title: ló, lovak, lovat: Two Words That Change

sections.title: The plural and the object of farm animals
sections.content: You know the plural *-k* and the object *-t* from A1. *tyúk* and *disznó* are regular: *tyúkok*, *tyúkot*, *disznók*, *disznót*. Two farm words are exceptions: *ló* gets a *v* before the ending (*lovak*, *lovat*), and *tehén* shortens its last vowel (*tehenek*, *tehenet*). Learn these two sets as they are.

items.english: I see three horses in the yard.
The cows are on the farm.
In the morning I feed the hens.

sections.content: After a number the noun stays singular, and the object ending stays too: *három lovat* ("three horses"), not *három lovakat*. With the definite *a*, a plural object is fine: *a lovakat*.
